reason: You bind the sharp flint firmly to the end of the branch with several tight turns of vine. It makes a crude spear, though the flint head may loosen or break under a hard thrust.
You lash the sharp flint crosswise to the end of the hazel rod with the vine. The springy haft and rough binding make a crude, usable chopping tool, though it will not take heavy blows well.
You bend the springy hazel rod into a bow and knot the short cord and vine together for its string. The joined string is awkward and uneven, but it holds the bow bent.

You tie the leather scrap between the short cord and the vine, shortening the longer side to make a crude sling. Its uneven, short cords make it awkward to use, but the leather can hold a small stone.
You saw through the crooked end of the branch with the sharp flint, shortening it to a stout, arm-length piece. The offcut falls to the ground.
You stitch the linen around a layer of straw, making a rough padded jacket. It is bulky and uneven, but wearable; Darin's linen is used up in the work.
You fold the linen around your head and tie it in place with the short cord, making a simple hood. The bolt belongs to Darin, and the cloth used in the hood is no longer part of it.
You tie the short cord across the back of the plank, making a loop you can grip. The wood is Tomas's, and your work alters it.
You tear narrow strips from the linen and roll them into a soft bandage. The bolt belongs to Darin.
You draw a length of flax thread through one of the iron needles’ eyes, ready for stitching. Mara’s needle and Hessa’s thread are used in the work.
You use the flint shard to cut two lengths from the fallen branch, then bind them together with the short cord. They make a crude splint, though the cord is short and the branch is somewhat crooked.
You crush the plantain leaves and yarrow together between your hands into a moist, fibrous poultice.
You creep up behind Tomas, who is absorbed in his work and does not see you coming, and swing the fist-sized stone into his head. The blow lands before he can react.
You thrust the branch at Bren before he sees it coming. Its blunt tip strikes his chest, but his mail shirt turns the blow aside.
You come up behind Darin and draw the sharp sword across his throat before he sees you. Darin does not survive this wound.
notes: Wound was fatal: the injuries added up (health reached 0).
